key_insight: Quantum resources constrain which function structures a model can approximate, while phase encoding can supply enough magic to make Clifford trainable gates sufficient on domains bounded away from zero.
engineering_relevance: Match gate resources to target-function structure, balancing approximation accuracy against encoding depth rather than relying on universality alone.
method: Analyze cumulative resource power of trainable gates for fixed encoding and readout.
Derive depth-independent bounds linking coherence to oscillation, imaginarity to odd components, and entanglement to distance from product functions.
Bound the encoding-depth overhead when replacing unrestricted trainable gates with Clifford gates.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports theoretical bounds for one- and two-qubit models and a polynomial depth-overhead guarantee, not empirical benchmarks.
watch_item: Clifford-only approximation relies on phase encoding and domains bounded away from zero; the depth overhead grows with inverse error and inverse distance from zero.
